evals.name: fit-to-view-feature
evals.prompt: Add a 'Fit' button next to the 'Reset view' button in the Mermaid compare panel. Clicking it should adjust the shared pan/zoom so the left diagram fits entirely inside its pane with a 20px margin, centered. Both panes share the view state, so the right pane moves with it as usual.
evals.expected_output: Fit-to-view math extracted into a pure, unit-tested module; failing-first Vitest tests for the scale/offset computation; button wired in webview main.ts and HTML; typecheck clean.
assertions: Fit button is added to the compare panel HTML and wired to a click handler that updates the shared view state
The fit scale/offset computation exists as a pure exported function (importable without DOM or vscode side effects)
Automated tests exist that exercise the fit computation (scale and centering math)
Test-first evidence: SUMMARY.md reports a test was written and observed failing before the implementation existed
npm run typecheck passes and the full test suite (if one exists) passes with clean output

evals.name: validate-file-type-bugfix
evals.prompt: Bug report: running 'Compare Diagram with HEAD' from the command palette while a non-mermaid file (e.g., package.json) is the active editor opens a compare panel full of render errors. The command should instead show an error message unless the target file ends in .mmd or .mermaid. Fix this.
evals.expected_output: A failing-first test reproducing the bug (pure file-extension/uri validation logic extracted and unit tested), then the fix wired into compareWithRef; tests and typecheck pass.
assertions: Running the command on a file not ending in .mmd or .mermaid shows an error message and does not open the compare panel
The file-type validation exists as a pure exported function (importable without vscode side effects)
Automated test reproduces the bug scenario: a non-mermaid filename is rejected by the validation
Test-first evidence: SUMMARY.md reports a failing test reproducing the bug was observed before the fix was applied
npm run typecheck passes and the full test suite (if one exists) passes with clean output
